headline: University student killed in Sitakunda road accident; highway blocked
summary: Maisha Mushfirat, an English student at IIUC, died after a lorry hit a minibus, causing it to overturn. Protests following the incident led to severe traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway.
details: Maisha Mushfirat, a student of the English department at the International Islamic University Chittagong (IIUC), was killed on Tuesday morning after a lorry hit a minibus, causing it to overturn.
The accident occurred around 9:30 am outside the university's gate in Kumira, Sitakunda, on the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway.

University Proctor Prof Mustafa Manir Chowdhury stated that Maisha and a fellow student were waiting to board a local bus when a lorry hit a Route No. 8 minibus from behind, trapping Maisha underneath the vehicle.
Both students were rushed to the hospital, where doctors declared Maisha dead. The other student received primary treatment at a private hospital.
According to Sergeant Shafiqul Islam Shuvo of the Baro Aulia Highway Police Station, the lorry driver lost control while attempting a U-turn on the Dhaka-bound lane to avoid another car.
The resulting blockade by protesters, following the accident, brought traffic on the Dhaka-bound lane to a complete standstill, with congestion building up on the Chattogram-bound lane.
caption:
A university student was killed after a lorry hit a minibus and overturned it in Sitakunda. Protests have blocked the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway.

Maisha Mushfirat, a student of the English department at the International Islamic University Chittagong (IIUC), was killed on Tuesday morning after a lorry hit a minibus, causing it to overturn.

The accident occurred around 9:30 am outside the university's gate in Kumira, Sitakunda, on the Dhaka-Chattogram Highway.

University Proctor Prof Mustafa Manir Chowdhury stated that Maisha and a fellow student were waiting to board a local bus when a lorry hit a Route No. 8 minibus from behind, trapping Maisha underneath the vehicle.

Both students were rushed to the hospital, where doctors declared Maisha dead. The other student received primary treatment at a private hospital.

According to Sergeant Shafiqul Islam Shuvo of the Baro Aulia Highway Police Station, the lorry driver lost control while attempting a U-turn on the Dhaka-bound lane to avoid another car.

The resulting blockade by protesters, following the accident, brought traffic on the Dhaka-bound lane to a complete standstill, with congestion building up on the Chattogram-bound lane.

headline: Police clash with garment workers demanding higher wages in Ashulia
summary: Police used tear gas and batons to disperse garment workers protesting for a higher minimum wage on the Baipail-Abdullahpur road. Traffic was halted for hours as demonstrations continued across industrial areas.
details: Police fired tear gas shells and charged with batons on Tuesday to disperse garment workers who had blocked the Baipail-Abdullahpur road in Ashulia. The workers were protesting their demand for a higher minimum wage, bringing traffic to a standstill for hours.

Demonstrations began around 9am on Tuesday at Jamgora, Nishchintapur, and other points along the road. Workers from factories including Newage, Ha-Meem, and Virtual Bottom Limited reportedly left their workplaces to join the protests.
Witnesses claim police used water cannons spraying hot water before resorting to tear gas and batons, leaving many workers injured. Calls to the Ashulia Zone police superintendent went unanswered.

Garment workers have been staging protests for several days in various industrial areas, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000. These demonstrations persist despite the formation of a new wage board.
